extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical investigators and institutional nominating officials applying for the Pew Biomedical Scholars program
extracted.subtask_description: Operational selection rubric for the Pew Biomedical Scholars fellowship, describing the program's evaluation components, eligibility thresholds, application requirements, program constraints, and selection process for early-career biomedical investigators nominated by institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding promise as contributor in science relevant to human health
rubrics_metrics.description: Outstanding promise as contributor in science relevant to human health — based on performance during education and training
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes demonstrated potential during education and training rather than solely later career metrics; used as a primary marker of future impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and pioneering approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative and pioneering approaches — to basic, translational, or applied biomedical research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that uses novel, pioneering methodologies or conceptual frameworks across basic, translational, or applied domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularly innovative approaches encouraged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that are especially innovative are explicitly encouraged, signaling that high novelty/innovation strengthens competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse field integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Diverse field integration — candidates whose work is biomedically grounded but draws concepts/theories from diverse fields are explicitly encouraged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary work that integrates concepts or theories from other fields into biomedically grounded research is favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful independent investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful independent investigator — demonstrated capability to lead a research program
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for evidence the candidate can run and sustain an independent research program (leadership, lab management, mentorship, securing resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill set needed to carry out high-impact proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill set needed to carry out high-impact proposal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the applicant possesses the technical, conceptual, and collaborative skills required to execute the proposed research successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable past accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable past accomplishments including: Honors and awards; Publications; Demonstrated research productivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past honors, publication record, and evidence of research productivity are used as signals of achievement and potential; considered as part of the researcher assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic exclusion: clinical trials research
rubrics_metrics.description: Does NOT fund clinical trials research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications proposing clinical trials are ineligible; applicants should not propose clinical trial activities as part of the funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard funding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard institutional/funder restrictions (e.g., allowable costs, compliance) govern use of funds; applicants must adhere to these but no special accounting restrictions are imposed by Pew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation balance: two-component assessment (Project and Researcher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-Component Evaluation: Component 1 — The Proposed Project; Component 2 — The Researcher
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is explicitly based on both the quality/creativity of the proposed project and the demonstrated promise and accomplishments of the researcher; both components carry considerable weight in committee deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on future trajectory rather than past output
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection emphasizes future trajectory rather than just past output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee focuses on the candidate's likely future contributions and trajectory; forward-looking potential is prioritized over a pure inventory of past achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: faculty rank and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant professor at start of award year; Appointment within previous 2-3 years
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be at the assistant professor level at award start and typically within 2–3 years of appointment; this is a threshold requirement—failure to meet it renders an application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: degree and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD, MD, or equivalent; U.S. institution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold a research doctorate or equivalent (PhD, MD, etc.) and be affiliated with a U.S. institution; institutional affiliation is a threshold condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may nominate only one candidate, which functions as an upstream competitive filter and affects institutional internal selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: Required materials include: Brief proposal (typically 5 pages), Specific aims, CV / biosketch, Two letters (including from department head), Institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should contain the listed items in the expected formats/lengths; department-head letter and institutional commitment are explicitly required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award size, duration, and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: $300,000 over 4 years (~$75K/year); Flexible use — research, equipment, salary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are sizable and flexible; applicants can request support for research costs, equipment, and salary without restrictive accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection body and process
rubrics_metrics.description: National Advisory Committee evaluates all applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standing national advisory committee reviews and deliberates on nominations; its judgments (including emphasis on person/trajectory) determine awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection funnel and acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: ~200 applications received per year (institutional nomination); 22 grants awarded (~11% acceptance rate)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High competition and limited slots (one institutional nominee) mean selection is selective; applicants should be prepared for a competitive internal nomination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative rubric orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew's rubric is heavily weighted toward person + trajectory rather than project specifics (similar to Searle, HHMI Investigator, and Sloan; contrasts with NIH/NSF)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing or tailoring applications, applicants should prioritize demonstrating investigator promise, career trajectory, and capacity to lead impactful research—less emphasis on exhaustive methodological detail than typical NIH/NSF proposals.
